newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.08 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.08 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.08 percent to close at 1.0256 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0255 to 1.0305 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0255 real and selling at 1.0305 reais in a morning auction.
The previous mini-band, set on Oct. 14, was between 1.0245 and 1.0295 reais to the dollar.
In the afternoon the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0255 reais per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market.
Dealers said preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Monday surplus of around $265 million in late afternoon, mainly due to strong financial buys.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.06 percent to end at 1.0311 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.070 per greenback, up 0.47 percent, traders said.
